Fourier Features Mapping (FFM) is a preprocessing technique that transforms low-dimensional input coordinates into a higher-dimensional space using sinusoidal functions to overcome the spectral bias of vanilla Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) [S1][S5, unofficial].

The claim states that Fourier Feature Mapping (FFM) is a preprocessing technique that transforms low-dimensional input coordinates into a higher-dimensional space using sinusoidal functions to overcome the spectral bias of vanilla MLPs. Source [S1] explicitly mentions that vanilla MLPs fail to capture high-frequency details (spectral bias) and that FFM transforms input coordinates into higher dimension vectors to address this. Source [S5] confirms that FFM projects d-dimensional input coordinates into a higher-dimensional space using sinusoids (cosine and sine functions) and that this makes the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) stationary, thereby enabling the MLP to learn high-frequency details early and fast, effectively overcoming the spectral bias issue where high-frequency components are learned slowly.
